claims.text: In situ microscopic mechanical testing will reveal localized deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Localized deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn are masked in bulk measurements.
The localized mechanisms provide evidence that microstructure contributes to enhanced ductility and strength.
The FeNiCrMn HEA has a complex microstructure with heterogeneous grain boundaries and phase distributions.
The proposed method is in situ micro-tensile or micro-compression testing coupled with digital image correlation or in situ SEM.
The testing is to be conducted at room temperature and conventional strain rates.
Grain boundaries, phase interfaces, and dislocation networks are the relevant local structural mediators.
High-resolution real-time imaging during microscale deformation can capture dislocation motion, localized plasticity, and potential twinning.
Dislocation motion, localized plasticity, and potential twinning underlie ductile behavior in FeNiCrMn.
These microscale deformation events are not observable in bulk tests.
The tests will show spatially heterogeneous strain fields and distinct localized deformation events correlated with microstructural heterogeneities.
Correlation between localized deformation and microstructural heterogeneity would indicate that the microstructure supports ductile deformation mechanisms.
Previous FeNiCrMn studies have focused mainly on bulk corrosion resistance and have included limited mechanical testing.
Previous studies have not resolved localized deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn.
Room-temperature results may not extend to high-temperature or non-standard strain-rate conditions.
Microscale behavior may not directly predict macroscopic mechanical performance.
The degree of correlation between microscale observations and bulk mechanical properties is uncertain.
Absence of distinct localized plasticity or microstructural deformation events beyond bulk-test observations would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of local behavior to correlate with enhanced ductility would falsify the hypothesis.
